claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(a) verbatim: 'Unless otherwise authorized by the President, only the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy, and Homeland Security, the Attorney General, and the Director of National Intelligence, or the principal deputy of each, may create a special access program. For special access programs pertaining to intelligence sources, methods, and activities (but not including military operational, strategic, and tactical programs), this function shall be exercised by the Director of National Intelligence. These officials shall keep the number of these programs at an absolute minimum, and shall establish them only when the program is required by statute or upon a specific finding that: (1) the vulnerability of, or threat to, specific information is exceptional; and (2) the normal criteria for determining eligibility for access applicable to information classified at the same level are not deemed sufficient to protect the information from unauthorized disclosure.'

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 1.7(a) verbatim: 'In no case shall information be classified, continue to be maintained as classified, or fail to be declassified in order to: (1) conceal violations of law, inefficiency, or administrative error; (2) prevent embarrassment to a person, organization, or agency; (3) restrain competition; or (4) prevent or delay the release of information that does not require protection in the interest of the national security.' Sec. 1.7(b): 'Basic scientific research information not clearly related to the national security shall not be classified.'

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(b)(4)-(5) verbatim: 'The agency head or principal deputy shall review annually each special access program to determine whether it continues to meet the requirements of this order. ... Upon request, an agency head shall brief the National Security Advisor, or a designee, on any or all of the agency's special access programs.' Note the National Security Advisor briefing is on request only, not automatic.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(a) permits establishment only where 'required by statute or upon a specific finding that: (1) the vulnerability of, or threat to, specific information is exceptional; and (2) the normal criteria for determining eligibility for access applicable to information classified at the same level are not deemed sufficient', and directs that these officials 'shall keep the number of these programs at an absolute minimum'.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(c) verbatim, in its entirety: 'Nothing in this order shall supersede any requirement made by or under 10 U.S.C. 119.' The executive order expressly subordinates itself to the statutory SAP oversight scheme, including the section 119(e) waiver.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(b)(6) verbatim: "For the purposes of this section, the term ``agency head'' refers only to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy, and Homeland Security, the Attorney General, and the Director of National Intelligence, or the principal deputy of each." SAP creation authority cannot be delegated below the deputy-secretary level.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: THE ISOO ACCESS CAP. Sec. 4.3(b)(3) verbatim: 'Special access programs shall be subject to the oversight program established under section 5.4(d) of this order. In addition, the Director of the Information Security Oversight Office shall be afforded access to these programs, in accordance with the security requirements of each program, in order to perform the functions assigned to the Information Security Oversight Office under this order. An agency head may limit access to a special access program to the Director of the Information Security Oversight Office and no more than one other employee of the Information Security Oversight Office or, for special access programs that are extraordinarily sensitive and vulnerable, to the Director only.' The executive-branch oversight body for the entire classification system can lawfully be reduced to a single individual for the most sensitive SAPs.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: EO 13526 sec. 4.3(a): 'Unless otherwise authorized by the President, only the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy, and Homeland Security, the Attorney General, and the Director of National Intelligence, or the principal deputy of each, may create a special access program.' For programmes pertaining to intelligence sources and methods, but not military operational, strategic and tactical programmes, the function is the DNI's.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 6.1(oo) verbatim: "``Special access program'' means a program established for a specific class of classified information that imposes safeguarding and access requirements that exceed those normally required for information at the same classification level."

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(b)(4) requires that 'The agency head or principal deputy shall review annually each special access program to determine whether it continues to meet the requirements of this order', and (b)(5) that 'Upon request, an agency head shall brief the National Security Advisor, or a designee, on any or all of the agency's special access programs.'

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: THE EXECUTIVE-SIDE NARROWING. Sec. 4.3(b)(3): 'An agency head may limit access to a special access program to the Director of the Information Security Oversight Office and no more than one other employee of the Information Security Oversight Office or, for special access programs that are extraordinarily sensitive and vulnerable, to the Director only.' The oversight body's access to an extraordinarily sensitive SAP can therefore be reduced to a single person, at the agency head's discretion.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 4.3(b)(1)-(2) verbatim: 'Special access programs shall be limited to programs in which the number of persons who ordinarily will have access will be reasonably small and commensurate with the objective of providing enhanced protection for the information involved. ... Each agency head shall establish and maintain a system of accounting for special access programs consistent with directives issued pursuant to this order.'

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 13526 - Classified National Security Information
claims.text: Sec. 1.7(a)(1) and 1.7(b) are the two provisions a whistleblower alleging an illegally concealed recovery program would invoke: (a)(1) makes classification to conceal a violation of law impermissible on its face, and (b) makes classification of basic scientific research not clearly related to national security impermissible. Neither carries an enforcement mechanism inside the order; the only remedy channel is the sec. 5.3 ISCAP / agency appeal process or the intelligence-community whistleblower statutes. Reasoning stated from the text.

edges.label: creates what the statute must report
edges.note: The order creates the object the statute reports on. EO 13526 sec. 4.3(a) is the authority to establish a special access program at all, and restricts it to six officials or their principal deputies: the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy and Homeland Security, the Attorney General, and the Director of National Intelligence. 10 U.S.C. 119 then obliges the Secretary of Defense to report the DoD ones to Congress. Creation is executive and unilateral; reporting is statutory. Both texts were read on 22 August 2026, and neither cites the other - the relationship is that one supplies the programmes the other counts.
